sources.entry: RocketChat - Free open source chat system for teams. An alternative to Slack that can also be self hosted.

summary.one_liner: An Electron-based desktop client for Rocket.Chat that runs on macOS, Windows and Linux and can connect to one or more Rocket.Chat servers.
summary.what_it_does: The app wraps the Rocket.Chat web client in a native desktop window for Windows, macOS and Linux, built with Electron. It supports multiple Rocket.Chat servers, which are listed in a sidebar and can be set through a servers.json file. Installers are published on the Releases page in several formats (NSIS/MSI on Windows, DMG/PKG/ZIP on macOS, AppImage/deb/rpm/snap/tar.gz on Linux). Administrators can override user settings with an overridden-settings.json file, for example to turn off auto-updates, hide the tray icon, or disable adding new servers for a single-server setup. The project is written in TypeScript and built with rollup, with Jest for unit tests and electron-builder for packaging.
use_cases: Use Rocket.Chat as a desktop app instead of a browser tab
Connect a desktop client to self-hosted Rocket.Chat servers
Deploy a single-server Rocket.Chat client to employees
Build and package a custom Rocket.Chat desktop installer
Pre-configure default servers for a team installation
notable: Overridable settings file lets admins lock down behavior such as auto-updates, tray behavior and adding servers
servers.json can bundle default servers into the installer, skipping the connect screen
Tag-driven release flow where CI builds all platforms and drafts a GitHub release
caveats: Minimum OS versions are Windows 10, macOS 12 and Ubuntu 22.04 or equivalent
Development requires Node.js 22 or newer and Yarn 4.0.2 or newer
